Definition: from G4862 and G1492; to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of:--consider, know, be privy, be ware of.
BiblicalUsage: Ananias keeps back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and lays the rest at the apostles' feet, and Paul says he knows nothing against himself, yet he is not justified by that, because the Lord is his judge. Knowing with another can be conspiracy, and knowing nothing against yourself can be self-deception, so the conscience needs a better judge than itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that my conscience is not my judge, and I believe only the Lord can acquit me, whether I know something against myself or not.
